QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_99

question.text: Nifty spot is at 24,000 and 3-month futures are at 24,300. After one month, Nifty spot is 24,500 and futures are at 24,650. Using Basis = Spot - Futures, how has the basis changed?

answer.text: Basis strengthened from -300 to -150, meaning the futures premium narrowed, which is expected as time to expiry decreases

explanation.text: The Logic: Step-by-step calculation: Initially: Basis = Spot - Futures = 24,000 - 24,300 = -300 After 1 month: Basis = 24,500 - 24,650 = -150 The basis moved from -300 to -150, i.e., it became less negative and closer to zero. When a negative basis moves toward zero, the basis is said to have strengthened. This corresponds to the futures premium narrowing, which is the expected convergence behaviour as time to expiry decreases. The Trap: The sign of basis here is negative (spot is below futures). A negative basis moving toward zero is described as strengthening (even though, descriptively, the futures premium itself is narrowing). The basis did not remain constant, nor did it have a positive value at the start. Note: Page 35 of the Series VIII workbook supports the basis sign convention (Spot - Futures), negative basis when futures exceed spot, and convergence of basis toward zero at expiry. Page 35 does not use the strengthen/weaken terminology itself; that terminology is the standard market convention applied to the basis values computed from the workbook formula.
